title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 1986 notes on topological realizations of 'réseaux' (networks, graphs, maps), Grothendieck introduces 'ficelles' (strings). From the neighbouring pages, a ficelle is a compact (triangulated) connected space X together with two disjoint closed 'extremities' A and B. A 'ligne' C is a separating subset. It cuts the ficelle into two ficelles F_{A,C} and F_{C,B}, and X is recovered by gluing them along C. An oriented ficelle is one whose origin A is fixed. For a line C, F_C is the set of lines of F_{A,C}. The relation C ≤ D iff F_C ⊂ F_D is a preorder. The top-left margin seems to warn that distinct lines C and D can give the same F_{A,·}. 'Lieux' (loci) are then plausibly the classes of lines up to this equivalence, so the preorder becomes an order.

This page states that the set L of lieux of an oriented ficelle is a poset with the following properties.
(a) It has a least element α (the origin) and a greatest element β (the end), with α ≠ β.
(b) For x ≠ β, the set {y > x} is downward directed (filtrant décroissant).
(b') For x ≠ α, the set {y < x} is upward directed.
(c) It is dense: x < y implies there is z with x < z < y ('divisibilité').
These properties make L a non-totally-ordered analogue of the interval [0,1]. They are what lets one approach a cut from above or below, e.g. via regular neighbourhoods of the cut.

NB 1: two disjoint lieux are comparable. Hence a finite family of mutually disjoint intermediate lieux is a totally ordered subset (a chain).

Main statement: the category of oriented ficelles F equipped with n mutually disjoint lieux x_1 < ... < x_n is equivalent to the category of chains (F_1,...,F_{n+1}; h_{21},...,h_{n+1,n}). Here the F_i are oriented ficelles and h_{i+1,i} : ex(F_i) ≅ or(F_{i+1}) are gluing isomorphisms (end of one piece identified with the origin of the next). This generalizes the n=2 statement of the previous page.

Margin NB 2: reversing the orientation replaces the order by its opposite.

The purpose is to develop a combinatorial-topological theory of 1-dimensional 'edges' with thick ends. This prepares the realization of the edges of a network by arbitrary connected compact triangulated spaces: the next page asserts that every connected compact triangulated space other than a point carries a ficelle structure. Structurally, the equivalence 'ficelle with n cuts = composable n+1-chain of ficelles' is a Segal-type condition. Oriented ficelles behave like morphisms (cobordisms from origin to end) in a category whose composition is gluing.
errors: NB 1 as transcribed ('deux lieux distincts, x<y ou y<x') would assert totality, which is false in general: lines can cross. The correct statement requires 'disjoint', which is what the image seems to say, with 'distincts' added. Only mutually disjoint families are chains.
Condition (b) needs x ≠ β (and (b') needs x ≠ α), otherwise the set is empty and cannot be filtrant. The insertion above line (b) presumably supplies this.

The directedness (b), (b') and density (c) are asserted without proof. They require some tameness of lines, e.g. bicollared or regular-neighbourhood boundaries in the triangulated setting. In a purely topological setting with arbitrary closed separating sets these could fail or need care.

The equivalence of categories implicitly requires that gluing two ficelles along an identification of end/origin again yields a ficelle, and that cutting along a line yields ficelles. This depends on the precise (here unstated) definitions of ligne and extremity.

ideas.what: Poset of 'lieux' (classes of separating cuts) of an oriented ficelle: bounded, with directed up/down sets, dense
ideas.modern_name: poset of separating cuts / slices; a non-total analogue of the order of level sets of a height function
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard source; resembles order-theoretic treatments of cuts in continua (e.g. separation order in continuum theory)

ideas.what: Ficelle with n disjoint cuts ≅ composable chain of n+1 oriented ficelles glued end-to-origin
ideas.modern_name: Segal condition / composition by gluing in a cobordism-type category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (Segal spaces, 1970s); cobordism categories: Atiyah, Segal, Galatius–Madsen–Tillmann–Weiss, Lurie

ideas.what: Reversing orientation gives the opposite order
Disjoint cuts are comparable, so mutually disjoint families form chains
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in continuum theory / separation theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck's ficelles with their gluing equivalence amount to a Segal-type category structure on general compact triangulated 'thick edges'. Morphisms are oriented ficelles and composition glues end to origin, so it is a 1-dimensional cobordism category whose morphisms are arbitrary connected polyhedra. This is a model for topological realization of networks, not an analogue of manifold cobordism.
missed.quote: La catégorie des syst. formés d'une ficelle orientée F et de n tels lieux x_1,...,x_n est équivalente à celle de systèmes (F_1,...,F_{n+1}, h_{21},...,h_{n+1,n}) de n+1 ficelles orientées, et des n homom. de recollement.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a Segal-space or cobordism-category formalism for realizations of graphs and maps by general polyhedra. This could bear on tame-topology approaches to dessins or ribbon graphs and on 'thick' geometric realizations of networks. The link does not appear to have been made explicitly.

missed.claim: The axioms (a), (b), (b'), (c) on the poset of lieux look like the start of an intrinsic order-theoretic characterization of ficelles, i.e. an abstract 'interval-like' poset. The characterization is not completed on this page.
missed.quote: Les lieux d'une ficelle orientée forment un L ordonné. Il satisfait aux conditions suivantes a) ... b) ... b') ... c) ... (divisibilité)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A classification of which posets arise as cut-posets of ficelles would be a small but genuine question in combinatorial topology / continuum theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary. Still, the page is an unpublished, explicit formulation of a Segal-type gluing equivalence for a homemade notion of 'string', together with an axiomatized dense directed poset of cuts. This is a coherent piece of an unpublished theory of topological realization of networks, though not a deep result.
transcription_corrections: NB ①: the words read as 'conditions [?] intermédiaires' should most likely be 'lieux intermédiaires, mutuellement disjoints, forment une partie totalement ordonnée' (continuation of a parenthetical about intermediate lieux).
NB ①: the first line reads roughly 'Deux lieux x,y disjoints [distincts], x<y ou y<x', with 'disjoints' underlined. The point is comparability of disjoint lieux.

Final sentence: 'La catégorie des syst. formés d'une ficelle orientée F et de n tels lieux x_1,...,x_n est équivalente à celle de systèmes...'. The inserted 'x_1,...,x_n' belongs with the n lieux, and 'orientée' qualifies the ficelle.
Line (b): the superscript insertion is likely the restriction 'x ≠ β' (the image shows '≠' with a Greek letter). The line (a) insertion is 'α et β, distincts'.
Margin ②: likely 'Si on renverse l'orientation, l'ordre est remplacé par l'ordre opposé'.
Top-left margin: the symbols read as '+_{A;C}' are probably 'F_{A,C}' / 'F_{A,D}'. It is a warning that F_{A,C} = F_{A,D} can occur for C ≠ D, motivating the passage from lignes to lieux.
